_meta.role: Native design declarations for the two combatant classifications and generalized mechanics; not an executable combat system or a per-creature migration.
_meta.designAuthority: Owner-approved direction dated 2026-11-12; individual mechanisms remain subject to design.
_meta.sourceBoundary: The existing Kaiju Fighting Lite rules are design reference material. These records do not reproduce the source, adopt its named procedures as universal mechanics, or distribute its licensed text.

entries.name: Standard and Complex Combatant Classification
entries.scope: An individual creature's statblock or combatant mechanics, independent of the encounter's other participants.

sharedFoundation.interoperability: Combatants of different models participate in the same encounter, use compatible timing and target/effect interactions, and can affect one another. Model-specific vitality, components, behaviors, and defeat rules may differ.
sharedFoundation.initiative: Both standard initiative and the optional Block Initiative are compatible; combatant model does not select initiative mode.
sharedFoundation.sharedGame: A model selection does not create an independent edition or contradictory set of game rules.

entries.name: Standard Combatant
entries.description: The ordinary statblock/combatant model. It participates fully in the shared encounter and retains normal creature-specific actions, traits, reactions, and other expressly granted abilities.
entries.ordinaryVitality: Ordinary Hit Points remain the expected baseline, subject to explicit creature and general-rule exceptions.
entries.specialFeatures: A Standard Combatant may have explicit triggered traits or other special abilities. The eventual boundary between those features and a Complex model has not yet been specified.
notImplied: Absence of meaningful tactics or special features
Small size or weak combat power
An alternative ruleset for the encounter

entries.name: Complex Combatant
entries.description: A statblock/combatant model that can define additional, creature-specific combat subsystems while remaining interoperable with Standard Combatants.

optionalCapabilityFamilies.scope: Individual targetable or destructible creature features or equipment, if explicitly defined.
Distinct damage/health pools or other damage pathways, if explicitly defined. Ordinary HP may also be retained.
Event- or condition-driven changes to available behavior, capabilities, or tactics.
Explicit requirements or sequences for defeat beyond the ordinary vitality outcome, if defined.

notMandatory: Kaiju anatomy, climbing, or other size-qualified rules
Targetable parts or multiple health pools
entries.configurationPolicy: Optional capabilities are not automatic grants. Which are available, and how they interact, must be declared by applicable native rules and combatant definitions; the precise schema is still open.

entries.name: Combatant Behavior and State Transitions
entries.scope: Creature-defined state and behavior changes, particularly for Complex Combatants; this does not establish a universal mandatory behavior profile.
entries.triggerPolicy: Each actual behavior transition requires an explicitly defined trigger. Damage thresholds, component changes, conditions, environment, choices, and other events are candidates, not universal thresholds.
entries.outcomePolicy: A transition may alter tactics, permissions, actions, defenses, resources, targets, or other expressly defined creature capabilities; it does not automatically apply a generic Rage or Rampage effect.
entries.ragePolicy: Rage or Rampage is only one possible creature-specific behavior. Other rage variants or wholly different state changes are permitted when authored.
entries.sequencePolicy: No global fixed phase ladder. Triggered states may be independent, conditional, reversible, or sequential when a creature's rules explicitly say so.
notYetDecided: State duration, stacking, concurrency, priority, and restoration
Source-qualified effects and changes to action availability
Eligibility of ordinary Standard Combatant features for this engine

entries.name: Size-Qualified Combat Mechanics
entries.scope: Mechanics whose fictional or physical requirements arise from creature dimensions, anatomy, or an explicit ability, rather than the Standard/Complex classification.
entries.principle: No size-based ability is implicitly granted by the Complex classification. Creature size and relevant morphology or grants qualify the actual mechanic according to its own rule.
exampleMechanicsForSeparateReview: Climbing onto, occupying, or traversing a sufficiently large creature
Interactions with body-scale anatomical targets or terrain-like creature surfaces
Exceptional reach, movement, trampling, or displacement defined by creature size and ability
notYetDecided: Applicable size categories and size differences for each mechanic
Specific action costs, reactions, and opposing checks
How targetable components interact with size-qualified positioning
